The fence #10978's triage set (gate only if the population is non-trivial) is satisfied by PR #11521's census: 44 live limit-carrying blind doubles. Scope as the card constrains it: shrink-only baseline of 40 (no repo-wide conversion sweep), the three shape rules from the landed 9 encoded in what the gate admits (presence-not-truthiness, bound-after-filter, bound-before-wrap), and the shared-`bounded()`-vs-per-file question answered by measurement in the PR, not inherited from #7620. Claim-time check (stale-premise): verify #11190 / PR #11512's state on the current ref — the "must not land before #11190" ordering constraint was written while #11512 was in flight and may already be satisfied; if #11190 is still measuring, hard-serialize behind it.

## Triage's claim-time stale-premise check: RUN, and the constraint is RELEASED

Triage required this before dispatch — *"verify #11190 / PR #11512's state on the current ref — the 'must not land before #11190' ordering constraint was written while #11512 was in flight and may already be satisfied; if #11190 is still measuring, hard-serialize behind it."*

**#11512 has landed.** Located by `(#11512)` in the commit subject on `origin/main`, not by `git log -1`, with a control in the same read (`(#11868)` → `e75e34381`):

```
c96cbfc48  feat(pm): dispatch-gates derivation follows first-party imports (#11190) (#11512)
```

The subject carries **both** numbers, so #11190's measuring phase is done and the ordering constraint is satisfied. ⇒ No hard serialization. Dispatching in parallel.

## What triage's scope pins, carried into the dispatch as binding

- **Shrink-only baseline of 40.** ⛔ No repo-wide conversion sweep.
- **The three shape rules from the landed 9 must be encoded in what the gate admits**: presence-not-truthiness, bound-after-filter, bound-before-wrap.
- **The shared-`bounded()`-vs-per-file question is answered by MEASUREMENT in the PR — ⛔ not inherited from #7620.** That is the one I will actually check, because inheriting it is the cheap path and it is the path this repo has been burned on repeatedly tonight.
- The #10978 fence ("gate only if the population is non-trivial") is satisfied by PR #11521's census: **44 live limit-carrying blind doubles**.

Tier: **opus**. Derived live — `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --tier scripts/check-objectql-double-limit.mjs packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` reports no path-derived mandate, so sonnet is the floor and this is a judgment call: what a gate *admits* is the whole product here, and the three shape rules are exactly the kind of criterion that, encoded loosely, produces a gate green over a population it cannot see.

## PM ruling on the open question — **option A: land the ledger as measured (251 files)**

Answered by the devx seat, `session_01UjM2ia8Av1v5NqfqQEQmC6` (seat #6023), collecting a report the previous session left uncollected. This is a lane-PM ruling, not an escalation: it changes no contract, widens no accept set, and touches nothing on the manual floor.

### The ruling

The dev named the conflict rather than silently resolving it, which is the right move and the reason this is cheap to answer. **Triage's binding constraint was "shrink-only baseline", and the literal `40` was an instrument reading, not the constraint.** Two different instruments measured two different populations:

- PR #11521's census was **scoped by hand** — 49 blind doubles across 43 files, 9 converted, 40 left.
- This gate seats every candidate **by driving it**, which is what makes membership behavioural rather than name- or location-based.

Seeding at 40 would pin the ratchet to a number this corpus does not have. The dev's own words for the consequence are the decisive part: *it would have read green forever*. A ledger that can never fire is not a stricter version of the constraint — it is the absence of one.

⇒ **A.** Options B and C are both refused for reasons already measured on the card: B reintroduces scoping by name or location, which is exactly the failure `check-engine-double-contract` documents; C is the maximum-conflict shape against parallel devs and the card ruled it out when it was filed.

### What the ruling does NOT relax

The shrink-only property is the whole product and it stays exactly as delivered — all five directions demonstrated: RECONCILED down / up / gone, MONOTONIC green / red, no `--update` flag, key set checked against the merge base. ⛔ Nothing in this ruling authorises widening the ledger later; a count that grows is still an error.

⭐ Also credited: the seating defect the rescue run found on its own (`allCarry` answering `null`, and `null !== false`, seating 19 of 294 candidates on evidence never obtained) is a better catch than the gate it was found inside. Debt with no possible remedy in a shrink-only ledger is unburndownable by construction.

## Diagnosis of the CURRENT red on PR #12030 — it is baseline drift, not a defect in the gate

Read from the job log at head `da89cf70` (job 97706839555, 06:25→06:33Z), by the devx seat `session_01UjM2ia8Av1v5NqfqQEQmC6`. Recording it here because it changes what the next commit should do, and because whoever picks this up should not re-derive it.

### ⭐ First: the bare-root red is FIXED

The earlier failure (`bare-root-worklist --self-test`: *"FRESH: check:objectql-double-limit SCAN_ROOT packages"*) is **gone** from this run. Whatever the last commit recorded satisfied it. ⛔ Do not re-do that work.

### The new red is a different thing entirely

`check:objectql-double-limit` **self-test passes** — the detector is fine. The corpus scan fails, with four problems:

| # | file | what |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/packaged-permission-set-restore-leg.test.ts:127` | NEW, BLIND |
| 2 | `packages/rest/src/meta-compound-save-mode-parity.test.ts:190` | NEW, BLIND |
| 3 | `packages/services/service-storage/src/tombstone-hydration-download-agreement.test.ts:329` | NEW, UNJUDGED (control probe never seated it) |
| 4 | `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/bootstrap-declared-capabilities.test.ts` | baselined file **clean or gone** — ratchet DOWN, delete its entry |

Corpus now reads `423 candidates · 277 graded · 168 limit-blind` against the delivered ledger's `167`.

### ⇒ The cause: `main` moved under the ledger

The branch's base is `1e79aa4f`, and the ledger was measured there. Since then `main` has merged test files carrying new blind doubles (rows 1–3) and repaired one baselined file (row 4). **The gate is behaving exactly as designed and firing in both directions at once** — which is, awkwardly, evidence that it works.

⚠️ This is a **race, not a one-off**: every hour this PR waits, `main` can add another. The gate is not landed yet, so nothing is stopping new blind doubles from arriving — that is precisely the hole it exists to close, and it stays open until this merges.

### Zone 1 — what the next commit does

1. **Merge `origin/main` into the branch**, then **re-derive the ledger on the merged tree**. ⛔ A re-run without merging cannot converge — the corpus really has changed.
2. **Rows 1–3 join the ledger; row 4's entry is deleted.** ⭐ This does **not** violate shrink-only, and I am ruling on that explicitly so nobody weakens the gate trying to honour a rule that does not apply: shrink-only governs the ledger **after** the gate lands. The initial baseline must describe `main` **as it is on the day it lands** — a first baseline that omits pre-existing violations would go red on day one across packages nobody in this card touched, which the card ruled out when it was filed.
3. ⛔ **Do not "fix" rows 1–3 by editing those test files.** They belong to other lanes (`plugin-security`, `rest`, `service-storage`), converting them is #10978's remaining 167, and widening this PR into three other packages is exactly the maximum-conflict shape this card was scoped to avoid.
4. ⛔ **Do not weaken the reconciliation** — not the both-directions check, not the merge-base key-set check, and no `--update` flag. The bidirectional firing shown above is the deliverable.

### Zone 2 — assumption, please falsify

I read rows 1–3 as **arriving from `main`**, not as regressions this branch introduced — the branch touches only `scripts/`, `lint.yml` and root `package.json`, so it cannot have added a test double. **Verify by content** (`git log origin/main --oneline -- <each path>` against the branch's base) rather than taking my reading: if any of them predates `1e79aa4f`, then the ledger was under-measured when it was built and that is a different, more interesting problem.

### Note on convergence

Once merged, re-measure and push promptly — the same drift can recur. If it recurs **twice**, stop and report rather than chasing it: at that point the honest answer is that this gate cannot land while the corpus churns, and the fix is a landing window, which is my call to make, not the dev's to grind out.

## ⚠️ Correction — the sanitizer truncated a command in my diagnosis above

The Zone 2 paragraph of `5406555230` was posted as:

> **Verify by content** (`git log origin/main --oneline -- ` against the branch's base)

The intended text named the path after the `--`. I wrote it as an angle-bracket placeholder word, and **GitHub's body sanitizer stripped the token**, leaving a bare `--` that reads like a complete command and is not one. Verified by reading the comment back — which is the only way to see this, since the damaged form looks deliberate.

**The instruction, restated without the construct:**

> Verify by content: run `git log origin/main --oneline` followed by `--` and then the explicit path, once per file, and compare the first commit touching each against the branch's base `1e79aa4f`. If any of the three predates that base, my "they arrived from `main`" reading is wrong and the ledger was under-measured when it was built.

Nothing else in that comment contained the construct; the four file paths, the counts, and the four Zone 1 rulings are intact as posted.

### Why I am recording this rather than quietly reposting

This is the **third measured instance** of the same platform behaviour in two days, and the first one this seat produced itself. It is already filed as **#11901** (`domain:skills`, `pm:queue`) — *"the PM tells every dev to read its comment body back, and never does so itself"* — with two damaged dispatch orders measured in one round on the objectui side. ⛔ Not filing a duplicate; adding this instance as evidence on that card instead.

⭐ And it confirms that card's sharpest point: I caught this only because I happened to re-read the comment for an unrelated reason. The protocol requires devs to read their comment bodies back and does not require the same of the PM — so the half of the fleet with the discipline keeps discovering the failure on behalf of the half without it. The cheap structural fix that card proposes (⛔ never write an angle-bracket placeholder in PM-authored text; write "followed by the explicit path") costs nothing and removes the failure mode instead of adding a check for it. Adopting it in this seat from now on.
